after.title: Reserve Bank of India: RBI imposes monetary penalty on Fusion Finance Limited
after.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 17, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹7.50 lakh (Rupees Seven Lakh Fifty Thousand only) on Fusion Finance Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of directions issued by RBI on ‘Know Your Customer (KYC)’ and ‘Internal Ombudsman’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under section 58G(1)(b) read with section 58B(5)(aa) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its financial position as on March 31, 2026. Based on the supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for failure to comply with the RBI directions.
After considering the company's reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty:
The company failed to obtain PAN or equivalent e-document thereof or Form 60 from customers, while establishing an account-based relationship with those customers; and,
The company failed to escalate the partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman for a final decision within the prescribed time.
This action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of this monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company.
(Brij Raj)
Chief General Manager

after.title: Reserve Bank of India: Reserve Bank issues Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026
after.summary:
The Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2015 were superseded by the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, which were issued on January 13, 2026, and became effective from October 01, 2026. The new regulations are principle based; intended to promote ease of doing business, especially for small exporters and importers; and empower Authorised Dealers to provide quicker and more efficient service to their customers.
Based on subsequent feedback received from stakeholders, the Reserve Bank has issued Amendment Regulations to Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 that were notified on November 02, 2026, and came into effect, retrospectively, from October 01, 2026 .
In this regard, to facilitate better understanding of the new trade regulations by the exporters/importers and other stakeholders, the Reserve Bank has placed a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 on its website.
(Brij Raj)
Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/1531

after.title: Reserve Bank of India: Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions
after.summary:
Today, the Reserve Bank released the second edition of its biennial Report titled “Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions”. The theme of this edition is ‘Local Finances and Capacity Building in Rural India’. Drawing upon a balanced panel of 2.25 lakh Gram Panchayats for the period 2022-23 to 2024-25, the Report presents an assessment of their finances and their role in achieving sustainable and inclusive rural socio-economic development.
Highlights:
Gram Panchayat finances strengthened during 2022-23 and 2023-24; they, however, remain dependent on intergovernmental transfers, accounting for about 90 per cent of total receipts, while own source revenues (OSR) accounted for a modest share of about 10 per cent, predominantly driven by non-tax receipts such as interest receipts, Panchayati Raj programme funds and user charges.
Expenditure patterns primarily reflected both the mandates of the Fifteenth Finance Commission and convergence with national schemes/missions, with water supply and sanitation accounting for the largest share (about 40 per cent) of total expenditure.
While notable progress has been made in rural connectivity, electrification, water supply, sanitation and community assets, inter-State disparities persist in access, quality and functionality.
As some large Gram Panchayats transition to small urban local bodies or Town Panchayats, functional responsibilities may expand faster than fiscal and administrative preparedness, requiring transitional fiscal support and administrative capacity building alongside a calibrated strengthening of OSR through improved collection efficiency and rationalised property taxes and license fees.
This Report has been prepared in the Division of Local Finances of the Department of Economic and Policy Research. after.summary:
In terms of GOI notification F.No. 4(4)-B(W&M)/2020 dated October 09, 2020 (SGB 2020-21 Series VIII - Issue date November 18, 2020) on Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme, premature redemption of Gold Bond may be permitted after fifth year from the date of issue of such Gold Bond on the date on which interest is payable. Accordingly, the next due date of premature redemption of the above tranche shall be on November 18, 2026.
2. Further, the redemption price of SGB shall be based on simple average of closing price of gold of 999 purity of previous three business days from the date of redemption, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd (IBJA). Accordingly, the redemption price for premature redemption due on November 18, 2026, shall be ₹13,499/- (Rupees Thirteen Thousand Four Hundred and Ninety-Nine Only) per unit of SGB based on the simple average of closing price of gold for the three business days i.e., November 13, November 16, and November 17, 2026.
Ajit Prasad
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)
Press Release: 2026-2027/1512

after.summary:
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 06, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹9.00 lakh (Rupees Nine Lakh only) on One Mobikwik Systems Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of the directions issued by RBI on ‘Prepaid Payment lnstruments (PPIs)’ and ‘Fraud reporting’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under the provisions of section 30(1) read with section 26(6) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its operations for the period from June 2025 to March 2026. Based on supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for its failure to comply with the said RBI directions.
After considering the company’s reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty:
the company had allowed fund transfer by certain PPI holders to non-pre-registered beneficiaries beyond the prescribed limit.
the company failed to report certain frauds within the prescribed timeline.
The action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company.
(Brij Raj)
Chief General Manager
